study_identification_part.si4_title: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are clearly stated, including the aim to introduce a methodological framework to parse neuroanatomical subtypes in autism using normative modeling and clustering, and the intended utility for understanding heterogeneity and clinical relationships.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here, we aim to introduce a novel methodological framework for parsing neuroanatomical subtypes within a large cohort of individuals with autism. ... Five biologically based putative subtypes were derived using normative modeling of CT and spectral clustering. ... These subtypes ... loaded differentially and more strongly onto symptoms and polygenic risk."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: NEW model built with a neurotypical reference cohort from EU-AIMS LEAP. Eligibility for NT cohort excludes intellectual disability; general MRI contraindications applied; additional exclusions (history of bipolar disorder or psychosis). Image quality control performed by visual inspection by at least 3 raters; scans with severe artifacts excluded; no manual edits allowed. Final NT sample size (N=206) and ASD sample size (N=316) reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"In order to obtain a normative reference, the participants with Intellectual disability were excluded from the NT cohort. ... Following the standard neuroimaging contraindications, individuals with claustrophobia or metal implants were excluded in addition to the Individuals who had a history of bipolar disorder or psychosis." 
"Prior to analysis, all surface reconstructions were visually assessed for reconstruction errors by at least 3 independent raters. We excluded a small number of scans with severe artifacts ... we did not allow manual edits..." 
"Here we included 206 neurotypical (NT) ... and 316 participants with autism ... across 6 sites from the EU-AIMS ... LEAP sample."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: 41398_2020_1057_MOESM1_ESM.docx.md — Supplementary Methods: Sample; Magnetic Resonance Imaging

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates include age and sex; nuisance covariates include full-scale IQ, site (dummy-coded), and FreeSurfer Euler number (scan quality). This addresses key covariates and site effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "for each participant, we estimated normative models to predict vertex-wise cortical thickness as a function of age and sex plus nuisance covariates including full-scale IQ, plus dummy coded site variables and the Freesurfer Euler number ... using Gaussian process regression."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data source for the reference cohort is specified as the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP), with participating sites listed and prior publications cited for design/characterization.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"... across six sites from the EU-AIMS multi-center Longitudinal European Autism Project." 
"Participants with autism were recruited from ... six study sites ... [KCL, Cambridge, Nijmegen, Utrecht, Mannheim, Rome]."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: PRIMARY data collection is used. Modality and sequence are specified (T1-weighted; ADNI sequence matched across sites), but specific acquisition parameters (e.g., TR/TE, resolution) and equipment specifications (manufacturer, field strength) are not reported.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "A high resolution T1-weighted image was acquired from each participant with a standard Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) sequence, matched across scanning sites."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described: FreeSurfer v5.3 used for CT estimation; visual QC by ≥3 raters; exclusion of scans with severe artifacts; no manual edits permitted; cortical thickness maps smoothed with 10-mm surface-based Gaussian kernel.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Cortical thickness was estimated ... using FreeSurfer version 5.3 ... Prior to analysis, all surface reconstructions were visually assessed ... We excluded a small number of scans with severe artifacts ... we did not allow manual edits ... Cortical thickness maps were then smoothed with a 10-mm surface-based Gaussian kernel."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For the NEW normative model, a data partitioning strategy is used: 10-fold cross-validation during training to obtain unbiased estimates.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We used 10-fold cross-validation during the training process to provide an unbiased estimation of the model."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals is described; analyses are confined to the LEAP cohort.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We included ... across 6 sites from the EU-AIMS ... LEAP sample." (No mention elsewhere of external healthy validation.)

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical model (Gaussian process regression) is clearly stated and covariates listed. However, key model settings (e.g., kernel type, hyperparameters) and implementation software/library for normative modeling are not specified.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text:
"... using Gaussian process regression." 
"Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to estimate a normative model of CT ... GPR was trained on the NT cohort ... using ... age, sex, FIQ, ... Euler number, ... site."
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: Zabihi2020.pdf.md — Methods; 41398_2020_1057_MOESM1_ESM.docx.md — Supplementary Methods: Normative modeling

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: For the NEW normative model, no quantitative performance metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, calibration/coverage) are reported for the reference cohort; while cross-validation is used, the paper does not present fit statistics for the normative models.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Methods describe model training and cross-validation but do not report quantitative fit metrics for the normative model.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.location: Zabihi2020.pdf.md — Methods; 41398_2020_1057_MOESM1_ESM.docx.md — Supplementary Methods: Normative modeling

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation is used, the characteristics (sample sizes and demographics) of the reference cohort in each partition (training/validation/test) are not described.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "We used 10-fold cross-validation during the training process ..." (No reporting of partition-level characteristics).

nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "... using FreeSurfer version 5.3 ..." (preprocessing). Normative modeling uses GPR with methods cited; no code or repository link provided.
